title: The 10 Best Corded String Trimmers
subtitle: Plug-in electric string trimmers and trimmer-edgers for lawns and weeds, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A corded string trimmer never needs a charge or a gas mix, and it costs less than a battery model of the same size. We ranked 10 best-sellers from BLACK+DECKER, WORX, CRAFTSMAN, Sun Joe and WEN on rating, review volume and features (a 5-amp or bigger motor, a 14-inch or wider swath, automatic or push-button line feed and an edger mode). All of them need an outdoor extension cord, sold separately. For battery trimmers, see our cordless string trimmer page.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 14-Inch 2-in-1 Corded String Trimmer and Edger with Auto Feed, 6.5 Amp (BESTA510)
products.verdict: The best seller and the most-reviewed corded trimmer on Amazon, with 16,306 reviews at 4.4 stars. A 6.5-amp motor, a 14-inch swath, automatic line feed and a wheeled edge guide cost $52.99.
products.best_for: Most yards within reach of an outlet that need trimming and edging.
products.skip_if: You need to work far from an outlet; a battery trimmer suits that better.
pros: 16,306 reviews at 4.4 stars; 1,000+ sold last month
cons: 6.3 lb, heavier than the 4 lb compact models

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 13-Inch Corded String Trimmer/Edger, 5 Amp (ST8600)
products.verdict: A 5-amp trimmer-edger with 5,127 reviews at 4.4 stars, the same rating as the BESTA510. It is about a pound lighter but has a smaller motor and a 13-inch swath, and at $59.00 it costs $6 more.
products.best_for: Buyers who want a lighter BLACK+DECKER trimmer-edger.
products.skip_if: You want the most power for the money; the BESTA510 is cheaper with a bigger motor.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 3-in-1 Corded String Trimmer, Edger and Mower Combo, 12-Inch, 6.5 Amp (BESTA512CM)
products.verdict: A 6.5-amp trimmer that clips into a 12-inch mower deck, so one tool trims, edges and mows a very small lawn. It has 9,741 reviews at 4.1 stars and costs $89.00.
products.best_for: Small lawns, patios and townhouse yards where a full mower is overkill.
products.skip_if: Your lawn needs a real mower; a 12-inch deck is slow on anything bigger than a small patch.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 14-Inch Corded String Trimmer with EASYFEED, 6.5 Amp (BESTE620)
products.verdict: The push-button version of the BESTA510: the same 6.5-amp motor and 14-inch swath, but you press a button to advance line instead of relying on an automatic spool. It is a pound lighter at 5.3 lb and costs $59.00.
products.best_for: People who want to control when line feeds out.
products.skip_if: You'd rather never think about line; the BESTA510 feeds itself for less money.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 13-Inch Corded String Trimmer, 4 Amp (BEST935)
products.verdict: The cheapest BLACK+DECKER corded trimmer here at $39.00, with a 4-amp motor, a 13-inch swath and automatic line feed. It rates 4.3 stars on 743 reviews.
products.best_for: Light trimming around a small lawn on a tight budget.
products.skip_if: You need a wheeled edger or power for thick weeds.
cons: No rotating head or edge guide listed

products.name: WORX 15-Inch 2-in-1 Corded String Trimmer and Lawn Edger, 5.5 Amp (WG119)

specs.extras: 90° pivoting head, telescoping shaft, flower guard

products.verdict: The widest swath here at 15 inches, with dual-line auto feed, a head that pivots 90 degrees for slopes and a telescoping shaft. It costs $49.99 and rates 4.0 stars on 986 reviews.
products.best_for: Larger yards and slopes where a wide cut saves passes.
products.skip_if: You want the strongest reviews; it sits at 4.0 stars.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN WEEDWACKER 14-Inch Corded String Trimmer/Edger, 6.5 Amp (CMEST913)
products.verdict: CRAFTSMAN's 6.5-amp, 14-inch trimmer with push-button feed, an edging mode and an adjustable-length pole. At $79.99 it costs $27 more than the BESTA510, which has the same motor rating and swath.
products.best_for: CRAFTSMAN owners and taller users who want an adjustable pole.
products.skip_if: You want value; the BESTA510 matches its motor and swath for $52.99.

products.name: Sun Joe 13-Inch Corded Electric Grass Trimmer and Edger with Telescoping Pole, 4 Amp (TRJ13STE)

specs.extras: Telescoping pole 41-50 in, flower guard, 0-45° head

products.verdict: A 4-amp trimmer-edger with a pole that telescopes from 41 to 50 inches, a flower guard and a head that rotates in 15-degree steps for edging. It has 2,136 reviews at 4.0 stars.
products.best_for: Tall users and gardens with beds to protect.
products.skip_if: You cut thick weeds; 4 amps is light duty.
cons: Listing sold by a third-party store (Spreetail)

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 12-Inch Corded String Trimmer/Edger, 3.5 Amp (ST4500)
products.verdict: A light 4 lb trimmer with a 3.5-amp motor and a 12-inch swath, rated 4.4 stars on 1,276 reviews. It uses bump feed, and at $54.20 it costs more than the bigger BESTA510.
products.best_for: Post-mow touch-ups where light weight matters most.
products.skip_if: You want auto feed or more power; the BESTA510 has both for less.
cons: Sold by a third-party store at $54.20

products.name: WEN Compact Corded String Trimmer, 10-Inch, 3 Amp (ET1003)

specs.extras: 37.5 in long; uses WEN ET-400 spool

products.verdict: The cheapest trimmer here at $31.94: a 4 lb, 37.5-inch compact model with automatic feed and a 10-inch swath. WEN sizes it for shorter users and small jobs.
products.best_for: Shorter users and small patios or fence lines.
products.skip_if: You have a full lawn to trim; 10 inches and 3 amps are small.

avoid.name: DEKOPRO 2.2A Corded String Trimmer Lawn Edger, 9-Inch
avoid.verdict: The weakest motor and narrowest swath in the search, sold as "powerful" for $69.99, $17 more than a 6.5-amp, 14-inch BLACK+DECKER.
reasons: Its 2.2-amp motor is a third of the BESTA510's 6.5 amps, and its 9-inch swath is 5 inches narrower, yet it costs $69.99 vs $52.99.
The title calls it "Powerful"; 11,000 rpm on a 2.2-amp motor is a no-load speed, not cutting power.
The listing says it pays out about half an inch of line every time you pull the trigger, so stop-start trimming uses up line fast.
The cheapest pick here, the $31.94 WEN, has a wider 10-inch swath.

buyers_guide.a: Corded trimmers cost less, weigh less and run as long as you like, but you drag a cord and stay within reach of an outlet. They suit small and medium yards. If your fence line is 150 feet from the house, a battery trimmer is easier.

buyers_guide.q: How many amps do I need?
buyers_guide.a: For a normal lawn, 5 to 6.5 amps handles grass and ordinary weeds. The 3 to 4 amp models are fine for edging and touch-ups after mowing but slow down in thick growth.

buyers_guide.q: What swath width should I get?
buyers_guide.a: The swath is the diameter the line cuts. 13 to 15 inches covers ground faster on a full yard; 10 to 12 inches is lighter and easier to steer around beds and posts.

buyers_guide.q: Auto feed, push-button or bump feed?
buyers_guide.a: Auto feed lets out line on its own, push-button feeds when you press a button, and bump feed needs you to tap the spinning head on the ground. Auto and push-button are easier for most people.

buyers_guide.q: What extension cord should I use?
buyers_guide.a: None of these include one. Use an outdoor-rated cord: 16-gauge is fine up to about 50 feet, and 14- or 12-gauge is the safer choice at 100 feet so the motor gets full power. Most of these trimmers have a cord-retention hook so the plug doesn't pull apart.
On a trimmer-edger the head rotates 90 degrees so the line cuts vertically along a sidewalk or bed. Models with a wheel or wire edge guide hold a straighter line than freehand edging.
